lectures.title: Backward classes and minorities: rights, bodies and welfare

items: Renamed as Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Minority welfare functions transferred to Ministry of Minority Affairs
**Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** deals with: SC welfare; OBC welfare; senior citizens; persons with disabilities; transgender welfare.
**Ministry of Minority Affairs** deals with: Muslims; Christians; Sikhs; Buddhists; Parsis; Jains.

parts.t: Backward classes: firsts and constitutional recognition
items: **First Backward Classes (BC / OBC) Commission:** Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953).
**First Chairman of BC Commission:** Kaka Kalelkar.
**First Mandal Commission Chairman:** B. P. Mandal.
**First Commission to Recommend 27% Reservation:** Mandal Commission.
**First Constitutional Recognition of OBC Reservation:** 1st Constitutional Amendment (1951).
**First State to Introduce Reservation:** Kolhapur State.
**First National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC):** 1993; the National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993 created NCBC.
**First Constitutional Status to NCBC:** 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2018; NCBC is the first OBC constitutional body (2018 constitutional status).
First to use social and educational criteria to identify backward classes; recommended caste-based census and reservations.
Identified 3,743 backward castes; formulated 11 social, educational, and economic indicators; recommended 27% reservation for OBCs.
Examined sub-categorization within OBCs in the Central List to ensure equitable distribution of reservation benefits among underrepresented groups.
**Bhikhu Ramji Idate Commission (2017):** target group Scheduled Castes (SC) & DNT; Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment; surveyed De-Notified, Nomadic, and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).
**Idate Commission and SEED:** it led directly to the formulation of the SEED Scheme.
**Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) (Mandal Case):** upheld 27% quota for OBCs; introduced the creamy layer exclusion; fixed the 50% reservation ceiling; ruled out quotas in promotions.
**Janki Prasad Parimoo v. State of J&K (1973):** clarified that caste alone cannot be the sole determinant of backwardness under Article 15(4); must include social and educational indicators.

parts.t: Schemes and portals for OBC / EBC / DNT
items: Umbrella scholarship & hostel scheme for OBC, Economically Backward Classes (EBC), and De-Notified Tribes (DNT).
Economic empowerment of DNTs via health insurance, housing, livelihood, and competitive exam coaching.
Direct online application platform for DNT community health insurance, coaching, and dwelling assistance.
Centralized scholarship application and disbursement system for OBC, EBC, and nomadic tribe students.
**First Constitutional Safeguard for Minorities / First Constitutional Provision for Minority Rights:** Articles 29 & 30.
**T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002):** unit for determining religious and linguistic minority status under Article 30 is the State, not the entire nation.
**First National Commission for Minorities (NCM):** established in 1992; the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992 establishes NCM.
**First Chairman of NCM:** Justice Mohammed Sardar Ali Khan.
Maintains religious character as on 15 Aug 1947
Protects minority educational rights under Article 30
**First National Data-Based Committee on Minorities:** Sachar Committee.
**First Commission on Religious & Linguistic Minorities:** Ranganath Misra Commission.
**Justice Rajindar Sachar Committee:** Prime Minister's High-Level Committee; assessed the socio-economic and educational status of the Muslim community in India.
**Sachar finding:** highlighted severe under-representation in public employment and higher education.
**Justice Ranganath Misra Commission:** the National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities (NCRLM), under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
**NCRLM recommendation:** 15% reservation for minorities (10% for Muslims) in education and government jobs.
**First National Integration Council:** 1961; first Chairman Jawaharlal Nehru.
Convergence of skill development, artisan support, entrepreneurship, and education for 6 notified minorities.
Free coaching and financial support for minority students clearing UPSC/SSC prelims.
Artisans' promotion, digital marketplace, and master trainer accreditation platform for traditional crafts.

lectures.title: Persons with disabilities, senior citizens and transgender rights

items: **First Constitutional Basis for Disability Welfare:** DPSPs + Equality Provisions.
**First Comprehensive Disability Law:** Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995.
**First Chief Commissioner for Disabilities:** created under PWD Act, 1995; the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is the first disability rights body.
**First National Trust Act for Autism, Cerebral Palsy etc.:** 1999.
**First National Institute for Empowerment of Persons with Multiple Disabilities:** established in 2005.
**First National Policy for Persons with Disabilities:** 2006.
**First Rights-Based Disability Law:** Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016.
Welfare of persons with autism, cerebral palsy, etc.
**National Trust Act, 1999:** legal guardianship and welfare provisions for Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, and Multiple Disabilities.
**Sudha Kaul Committee (2010):** Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment; drafted the initial replacement bill for the PwD Act, 1995.
**Aim of the Sudha Kaul draft:** aligning India's domestic legal architecture with the UNCRPD (culminating in the RPwD Act, 2016).

parts.t: Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016
items: **Date of enforcement (commencement):** April 19, 2017; replaced the 1995 Act.
**Categories:** recognizes 21 categories of disabilities (expanded disability categories from 7 to 21).
**Reservation:** mandates 4% reservation in government jobs (public employment) and 5% in higher education for benchmark disabilities.

**Rajive Raturi v. Union of India (judgment of 2017, reported 2018):** framed concrete directions for time-bound visual, auditory, and mobility accessibility in public transport and built infrastructure under the RPwD Act.
**Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021):** scribe facility cannot be restricted only to persons with benchmark disabilities.
**Reasonable accommodation:** Vikash Kumar recognized "reasonable accommodation" as an intrinsic component of equality.

parts.t: Schemes and campaigns for persons with disabilities
items: Universal accessibility in built environments, transport systems, and ICT ecosystems.
National centralized database and single identity card for delivery of welfare benefits.
Free distribution of modern aids and assistive devices for rehabilitation.
**Accessible India Campaign as an awareness campaign:** nationwide public campaign auditing and retrofitting public spaces for barrier-free physical and digital access.

parts.t: Digital platforms for persons with disabilities
items: Centralized issuing of Unique Disability IDs and digital disability certificates for seamless welfare access.
Crowdsourcing accessibility complaints regarding public buildings, transport, and infrastructure.
Pre-assessment holistic screening tool used by school teachers to identify 21 disabilities under the RPwD Act, 2016.
Online digital library delivering accessible books in formats like DAISY, audio, and Braille.
Dedicated portal for skill development, vocational training, and employment listings for Divyangjan.
**Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007:** target group Senior Citizens & Family; legal obligation on adult children/heirs to provide maintenance.
**Maintenance Tribunals:** the Act establishes and empowers Maintenance Tribunals.
**NALSA v. Union of India (2014):** recognized transgender individuals as the Third Gender; affirmed their fundamental right to self-identify their gender identity.
**Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018):** decriminalized consensual same-sex adult relationships by reading down Section 377 of the IPC.
